title: "Part 3 – Reproduction and exploration"

**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/trust-one-day.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).

Part 3 has two hands-on tasks, the reproduction and a first exploration of the menu of alternatives, with the talk that connects them in between.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, Part 3 | The instruction of Task 2 of Multi100 read word for word, what it left open, and the aim of the reproduction: the three-level model that analyst 6U3LL fitted to the file that Multi100 gave the analysts. | 10 minutes |
| Task 3 in your report or working script, or [Browser lab](../../cases/trust/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) Task 3 | In the workspace, `fetch_multi100()` makes sure that the file of the analysts is in place, and the chunk of Task 3 fits the model of Table 3 of the paper without the unemployment rate, with random intercepts for countries and country-rounds, using `lme4::lmer()`. It should give *t* = 46.625 on 72,733 respondents, the value that Multi100 recorded for 6U3LL. Everyone types their value without sending it and sends it when the facilitator says go, so that the identical values appear at the same moment. The browser lab cannot read the file from the OSF, so it shows the reproduction as the course pipeline computed it with the same code, beside that code, and reads the closest specification of the course on the course data from the curve, which gives 0.174. | 20 minutes |
| Slides, the file and the model | What the number depends on: an intercept for every country-round gives the same coefficient on the same file, while the same specification on the course extract gives 0.174, because the two files code the vote controls differently. Then the two rebuilds of the data from the survey files, by SCORE and by the course, which part ways over the coding of the two vote controls; and why everyone in the class got the same value while the five analysts, each writing their own code, did not. | 8 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../cases/trust/menu.qmd) and slides | The twelve decisions at three levels, the five on which the curve keeps more than one option, the 192 specifications that they make, and the ground rules for the menu: change one decision at a time, and read the reason when an option is refused. | 12 minutes |
| Slides, the methods | Comparisons within country-rounds, fixed against random intercepts, and attitude scales against their single items. An optional run of five slides takes the statistics further: reliability by country, survey weights, missing answers and the size of the sample, satisfaction with the government as a control, and effect sizes on one scale. | 15 minutes |
| Task 4 in the workspace or on the [Browser lab](../../cases/trust/lab.qmd#task-4-menu), then [Multiverse](../../cases/trust/multiverse.qmd) | Call `try_spec()` with no arguments for the reference specification, then three or four times more, changing one argument at a time, and print the tries side by side with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for an option off the curve, such as `concern = "culture"`, to read why it is refused. Then rerun the one that you would defend and send it with `submit_exploration()`. Your mark is drawn on the class chart as an open circle. | 25 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have reproduced *t* = 46.625 yourself and know that the file, not the model, separates it from the course data; you have tried three or four alternatives one argument at a time; and you have put an exploratory mark on the class chart.
